title: Constant rate: rate × time (or amount ÷ rate)
subtitle: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units · 17 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **17 of the official questions in Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units are this one** — 11 Easy, 4 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question gives one 'per' quantity (items per hour, a speed, a price per unit, space needed per person, an exchange rate, days per cycle) and asks for a total, a time, or a count.
- Look for words like 'at this rate', 'constant speed', 'every ___ days', 'at least ___ per person', or 'how many times could you fill...'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Decide which of total, rate and count/time is unknown.
- 2) Total = rate × count; count = total ÷ rate.
- Let the units tell you whether to multiply or divide.
- 3) Then do any leftover step the question adds, such as a difference between two totals, a fee taken off, or rounding down to a whole number.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: It's a single multiplication or division, so use it as a calculator.
For 'maximum number' questions, you still have to take the floor yourself.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You answer an intermediate value instead of the final one: the converted amount before the fee, or one moon's total instead of the difference.
Another trap is multiplying when the units say to divide.
In 'at least ___ per person' or 'completely fill' questions, you round up when you have to round down to a whole count.
